The data also lets us compare criminal history at time of arrest vs. current status. The short version: most people's records don't change much but when they do, outcomes tend to get worse for non-citizens.
For the first time, this data lets us map arrests by specific ICE field office not just broad regions. Of 78,500 arrests in 2026 so far, I mapped 75,333, giving us 96% geographic coverage.

West Virginia is a striking outlier that deserves more attention. ICE arrests there surged dramatically between October 2025 and February 2026. I haven't seen much reporting on this and the data says we should be paying closer attention.

The data shows ICE is strategically targeting specific regions. Minnesota spiked in January (Operation Metro Surge). Illinois spiked in October (Chicago enforcement surge). Both driven largely by people with no criminal history.
The biggest driver? Arrests of people with NO criminal history. "Other immigration violators" (people with no charges or convictions) continue to make up the largest share of ICE arrests.
Despite public safety justifications for mass deportation, monthly ICE arrests have not increased substantially since Spring 2025. In fact, arrests have objectively declined since October 2025.
First, the data now goes back to October 2022 further than the previous release. It covers through March 9, 2026, giving us the most complete picture of ICE enforcement we've had yet.
New ICE arrest data just dropped via the Deportation Data Project's FOIA lawsuit. I spent hours validating it so you don't have to. Here's what the numbers actually show. 🧵

This is what immigration enforcement looks like at scale 11,000 American children and counting.

In my research, I've documented how enforcement policy creates cascading harm far beyond the individual. This data confirms it: schools, churches, and child-welfare systems are absorbing the costs of federal decisions.

ICE quietly renamed its own parental guidance policy from the "Parental Interests Directive" to the "Detained Parents Directive." The name change signals a shift in priorities, not a protection of families.
Many of these parents had no criminal record beyond immigration or traffic offenses. Empty desks at school, emergency foster placements, and overwhelmed nonprofits are the real-world result.

Under Trump, mothers of U.S.-born children are being deported at roughly 4x the daily rate seen under Biden. Nearly 60% of arrested parents faced removal compared to 30% under the previous administration.
Researchers matched ICE arrest reports with deportation records. The data covers late 2021 through mid-August 2025 and was secured through public records requests by the UW Center for Human Rights.
A new analysis of federal records reveals ICE detained parents of at least 11,000 U.S. citizen children in just the first 7 months of Trump's second term. 🧵

Each of these actions may be technically legal. But together they form a pattern: billions in public money, moving fast, in the dark.
